clue.text: Finished article with workplace in disarray

parts.note: something finished is all over
the definite article
a shop is a place of work, as in a workshop or shop floor

explanation.surface: A completed news piece lands on a chaotic office.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered everywhere in a muddle, so it describes things in disorder.

clue.text: Great-grandad was heartlessly involved in hostilities

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
heartlessly tells us to remove the central letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An elderly relative once took part in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips the middle A from WAS, leaving WS; 'involved' then shuffles GREATGRANDAD with WS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties openly hostile and ready to fight, so it means engaged in hostilities.

clue.text: Tract of grassland farmer initially rented

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word farmer

parts.note: let means rented out

explanation.surface: A farmer leases out a stretch of pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a piece of land beside 'grassland', but it is a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, which is a synonym for a printed handout.

clue.text: Clear the chamber

definitions.meaning: to clear an obstacle is to jump over it, as a pole-jumper does
an arched underground room or strongroom

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to leap over something and an underground room such as a cellar or crypt.

clue.text: Over-luxuriant heather is causing annoyance

parts.note: rank describes vegetation growing too thickly
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Overgrown heather on someone's land is irritating them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment, so the participle means irritating.

clue.text: Poet's garden invaded by driving club

definitions.note: read as 'the poet is', so it names a single poet

indicators.note: invaded by means the club gets inside the garden word

parts.note: to hoe is to work the garden soil
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A poet's garden has been overrun by golfers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving club' suggests golf; it is the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring body.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a celebrated Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: A crowd participating in ecstatic ceremony

indicators.note: participating in places the crowd inside the word for ecstatic

parts.note: sent is old slang for enraptured or carried away
to cram is to crowd or pack in

explanation.surface: A throng joins in a rapturous ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a religious rite, such as baptism or communion.

clue.text: Work on a place that is incomprehensible

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a quality or thing that cannot be understood

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a city is a place

explanation.surface: Someone toils at a baffling location.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is obscurity of meaning, the quality of being hard to understand.

clue.text: A part of geese I'd fancy

definitions.text: A part of geese I'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb of invention signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner says which bit of the goose they would like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the luxury paste is made from the fattened liver of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: This luxury pâté is made from goose liver, a part of geese one might well fancy.

clue.text: Avoid paying for kebab, grabbing an extra?

indicators.note: grabbing means the kebab word takes hold of the other pieces

parts.note: a doner is a kebab
in cricket a run scored by byes or wides is an extra

explanation.surface: A diner skips the bill for a kebab and nabs something more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat. The British idiom means to flee without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang idiom means to leave secretly, typically without settling a bill.

clue.text: Butt and tips of cigarettes lying around revolting ashtray

indicators.note: tips are the ends, here the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A cigarette end and ash spill from a disgusting ashtray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a cigarette end beside the ashtray; it is Dame Clara Butt, the English contralto.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Clara Butt was a famous English contralto, so her first name goes with her surname.

clue.text: Body-warmer — clothing I lately put away

annotationWithheld.why: Body-warmer — clothing I lately put away (5): no fair parse found for G and E/T; 'put away' and 'lately' give no standard letters building GILET
annotationWithheld.clue: Body-warmer — clothing I lately put away

clue.text: Profitable move to revictual

indicators.note: move signals that the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restocking with food turns out to be a money-making step.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative is a direct synonym for producing much profit.

clue.text: Hospital department — after a short time one is put in one's place

indicators.note: after places one behind the abbreviated hour

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: After a brief wait, a patient is shown to a seat in the hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in one's place' suggests a rebuke; here it is the throne, the monarch's place.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthrone is to place a monarch on the throne, their rightful seat.

clue.text: Travel on the Circle Line?

parts.note: a London Underground line running in a loop brings you back to where you started

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line that runs in a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back again is what riding a looped line amounts to.

clue.text: Repeat work in pool — soak before last of compulsory exercises

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word compulsory

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A swimmer soaks in the pool before mandatory drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' suggests swimming; it is a typing pool, an office of typists.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing pool is a team of typists, so repeated work there is keying a document again.

clue.text: See upstanding English eating places get humiliated

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the words are read upwards

parts.note: cafes are places to eat

explanation.surface: Someone is shamed by the sight of English restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb of the surface; it is the old exclamation 'lo!'. 'upstanding' reads the eating places and English upwards, giving SEFACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is the idiom for suffering humiliation or loss of respect.

clue.text: Put forth from Brussels

definitions.meaning: to grow new shoots or buds
a Brussels ... is the small cabbage-like vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to send out shoots, and it completes the name of the Brussels vegetable.

clue.text: Malignant creature — repel it violently

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty animal is driven off with force.
explanation.definitionFit: A reptile is figuratively a mean, treacherous person, as well as a creature like a snake.

clue.text: Postponement of payment but not for dance

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A debt is deferred, though not for the sake of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Contango is a Stock Exchange term for a fee paid to defer settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old London Stock Exchange contango was carrying settlement over to the next account, a deferral of payment.

clue.text: Nothing about set attracts a girl

indicators.note: about means the word for nothing wraps round the other piece

parts.note: nil means nothing
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A film set holds no appeal for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella is a girl's name, as borne by the cookery writer Nigella Lawson.

clue.text: Talk at length, with great accuracy

definitions.meaning: a phrasal verb for speaking tediously and at length

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to talk on and on and, as slang, spot on or exactly right.

clue.text: Regarding the sweet I had to refuse

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
pud is short for pudding, a British word for dessert
ate means had, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone declines dessert, having already eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: PUD is British slang for pudding, the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or refuse to accept something.

clue.text: Bird dog's not black

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the letter for black

parts.note: read as 'dog is'; a beagle is a breed of dog
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The hound isn't a black one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Give cry of pain after butt

indicators.note: after puts the cry behind the word for butt

parts.note: the butt is the end of something
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps after being headbutted.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or a quality to someone.

clue.text: Humming sound used to be heard by some

indicators.note: heard by some signals that in some accents the word is spoken like the answer

parts.note: were is a past form of be

explanation.surface: A buzzing noise once existed, and some people could hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard by some' admits that only some speakers say WERE like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the continuous buzzing noise of something spinning fast.

clue.text: Kind of fever, affecting the throat, covering the country

indicators.note: covering means the throat word goes round the country

parts.note: gular is an anatomical word meaning of the throat
land is a country

explanation.surface: An illness affecting the throat spreads across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Glandular fever is the British name for mononucleosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Glandular fever is a viral illness, so the adjective names a kind of fever.

clue.text: A Wren's perked up amazingly, in shroud

indicators.note: amazingly signals the letters are rearranged in a surprising way

parts.note: read as 'Wren is', so the S counts

explanation.surface: A member of the Women's Royal Naval Service cheers up remarkably while wrapped in a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren is a member of the former Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: To shroud something is to conceal it, which is to keep it secret.
